assertions.assertion: A charger reports a security event with SecurityEventNotification.req carrying a required type (string[50]) and dateTime timestamp and an optional techInfo (string[0..255]); the CSMS confirms receipt with the empty SecurityEventNotification.conf. The bridge keeps the type verbatim and the timestamp's instant, including a non-UTC offset.
behavioural_evidence_pending: storage-failure InternalError path: proven in the application tests only (a_failed_write_leaves_the_snapshot_unchanged_and_the_gate_keeps_its_shed_calls), not in the daemon tests
the uob events command is not exercised; the HTTP event stream it reads is

assertions.assertion: The charger queues security events with guaranteed delivery while disconnected, so the CSMS must expect redelivery of an event it already acknowledged. This is a charger-side obligation; the bridge's deduplicated acknowledgement of identical redelivery is bridge design, not a requirement text.
behavioural_evidence_pending: redelivery after journal retention pruned the first record is proven in the storage tests only (a_pruned_event_is_no_longer_recorded)
the next stored record carrying shed_calls after a flood window is proven in the application gate tests, not in the daemon tests

assertions.assertion: The 21 standard security event names are spelled as in section 8 and flagged critical or not as listed there; a type outside the list (up to 50 characters) is still a valid notification and is kept verbatim as a vendor type.
behavioural_evidence_pending: the daemon tests sample three standard names and the vendor types; all 21 names are checked in the application unit test only

assertions.assertion: techInfo may carry operator-supplied text up to 255 characters, including the recommended user and origin layout for maintenance logins. The whitepaper does not forbid credentials in techInfo, so a bridge must treat the field as untrusted; the credential fixture uses obviously fake values.
behavioural_evidence_pending: known limits: a short secret with no label, natural-language phrasing such as password is x, other encodings and Digest parameter lists are not detected; long mixed-case identifiers and hex fingerprints are redacted although they are not secrets

assertions.assertion: ExtendedTriggerMessage.req carries a required requestedMessage from the seven MessageTriggerEnumType values and an optional connectorId (> 0); ExtendedTriggerMessage.conf answers Accepted, Rejected or NotImplemented.
behavioural_evidence_pending: a partial observation (some targets observed, the deadline passed) is not tested
a BootNotification trigger before acceptance is proven in the protocol adapter tests only

assertions.assertion: ExtendedTriggerMessage with FirmwareStatusNotification triggers a SignedFirmwareStatusNotification, not the legacy FirmwareStatusNotification: Idle when the last sent status was Installed, otherwise the last sent status. A plain FirmwareStatusNotification therefore never satisfies this trigger.
behavioural_evidence_pending: the Idle-after-Installed choice is the station's (L01.FR.28/29) and is proven on the simulator model only; the bridge accepts whichever signed status arrives

assertions.assertion: ExtendedTriggerMessage with LogStatusNotification triggers a LogStatusNotification.req whose requestId may be omitted only when no log upload is ongoing; the bridge accepts that Idle report as trigger evidence while keeping its job reconciliation by exact requestId.
behavioural_evidence_pending: an Uploading report with a requestId in answer to a trigger is proven on the simulator model only

assertions.assertion: A connector-specific trigger names a connector greater than zero; a station-wide trigger omits connectorId. Zero and negative connector numbers are schema-valid integers but violate the 5.5 constraint, so the bridge refuses them itself before anything is sent.
behavioural_evidence_pending: at the management HTTP surface a non-positive connectorId is refused as 400 command.invalid_schema_or_payload before the adapter's InvalidParameters applies

assertions.assertion: SignChargePointCertificate is a legal wire value but triggers a SignCertificate.req, which belongs to certificate management (issue #129); the bridge refuses it as unsupported and never sends it.
behavioural_evidence_pending: at the management HTTP surface SignChargePointCertificate is refused as 400 command.invalid_schema_or_payload because the offered descriptor lacks the value; the adapter's UnsupportedOperation is proven in the registry and adapter tests

not_covered: charger-side A04.FR.04 security-log storage and the contents of the security log (issue #127 only receives notifications; log retrieval is covered by the diagnostics fixtures)
security profiles and their transitions (A00, A05; issues #345 and #346)
certificate management, SignCertificate, CertificateSigned and other certificate messages (issue #129)
triggering SignChargePointCertificate: refused as unsupported until issue #129
OCPP 2.0.1 security events (issue #128); the bridge keeps answering them NotImplemented
physical hardware, production artifact storage or OCA certification
execution_status: Fixture corpus validated against the pinned Whitepaper Edition 4 schemas. Each assertion's behavioural_evidence names the contract, application, storage, protocol, actual-daemon and simulator tests that prove it in isolated software verification, and its behavioural_evidence_pending lists what those tests do not prove (key name kept for the corpus test; it now holds remaining gaps only). Not proven at service level: the storage-failure InternalError answer (application tests only), a partial trigger observation, redelivery after journal pruning, shed_calls on the record after a flood window, and the uob events command. The opt-in separate-process joint smoke (bins/uob-sim/tests/security16_joint_smoke.py) ran outside the workspace verifier. Software verification only, not hardware interoperability or OCA certification; the ocpp16.monitoring-security.security-events and ocpp16.monitoring-security.extended-trigger rows are verified and the parent ocpp16.monitoring-security row stays planned for the security-profile half (issues #345 and #346).
